title: Banque des Républiques raises taux directeur to 5.75 per cent as livre pressure persists
content: The Banque des Républiques raised its taux directeur by half a percentage point to 5.75 per cent on Wednesday, the fourth increase in twelve months, citing services inflation that has held above 4 per cent since the spring and wage settlements it described as “incompatible with the convergence path”.

In its communiqué, the Comité de politique monétaire voted seven to two in favour of the increase. The minority argued that the tightening comes too late to influence this year’s price cycle and risks deepening the slowdown in construction and small manufacturing, where credit costs have doubled since 2024.

“We are not yet at the point where the livre needs emergency defence, but we are no longer in a position to look through inflation,” Governor Marguerite Salvat told a press conference. She confirmed that the bank had intervened twice in the past fortnight to smooth the currency’s fall, without disclosing amounts.

The immediate effect was felt in the debt market. Yields on ten-year dette souveraine rose six basis points intraday before easing, and the spread with the reference basket widened modestly. Mortgage rates at the four largest banks were expected to reach their highest level in a decade by December.

Finance Minister Ivan Rogier said the government would “take the central bank’s decision into account” in the autumn budget, a formulation read in the Assembly as an admission that planned infrastructure spending will be trimmed. The opposition accused the government of having exhausted its fiscal room through last year’s tax reductions.

Economists at the Université d’Aurelle now expect growth of 1.1 per cent next year, down from an earlier forecast of 1.6 per cent, and warn that a rising taux directeur combined with a weak livre historically produces a sharp compression in imports, with visible effects on consumer prices by the second quarter.

The Comité de politique monétaire meets next on 16 December. A majority of analysts surveyed this week expect a pause, though two investment houses retain the view that a further increase of 25 basis points is likely if services inflation stays above 4 per cent in November.
author: Marc-Antoine Rivière, rubrique économique — Agence Continentale
